subject: Deprecation dependency map + customer comms template — intake for exceptions
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Deprecation dependency map + customer comms template — intake for exceptions

Team —

Quick ask to align on the migration coordination for the upcoming API/model deprecation we announced last week. I want a single place we can hand to customers (and internal CSMs) that explains: what will change, which endpoints/variants are affected, a dependency map (client usage, SDKs, integrations), and a canonical comms template.

Please take the following as the minimal deliverables for Monday EOD (US):
- A dependency map for your area (use the attached XLS template). Focus on: endpoints, model variants, SDK calls, and known third-party integrations.
- A customer-facing comms template (short + long versions) we can AB test.
- An exceptions intake form we can point customers to; include a clear SLA for reviews.

Notes / constraints:
- Target migration window starts 2027-01-15; customers should see a 90-day lead time.
- Any compatibility blockers (embeddings format change, API contract delta) should be flagged as "high" and include an expected mitigation.
- If you need to escalate exceptions to Product or Legal, copy me + Priyom on the intake.

Attachments: dependency-map-template.xlsx, comm-template-v1.md, exceptions-intake-form.pdf

Thanks —
Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Sr. Program Manager, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Copying Product notes into thread to make the asks concrete.

Key product clarifications you should pick up in the dependency map:
- Mapping: list exact model variant -> new recommended variant (e.g., gen-v1-alpha -> gen-v2-stable). Include confidence band and any behavioral deltas (output format, tokenization differences).
- Compatibility gates: embeddings shape and checksum changes, streaming protocol version, and any function-calling schema changes.
- Rollout options: auto-redirect (server-side shim), client SDK helper (minor SDK bump with warning), or strict-422 after migration window. Each has different comm framing.

Blockers we've already seen from pilot customers:
1) Large enterprise customers using pinned quantized variants — they need a compatibility shim for KV cache format.
2) Partners that proxy requests via a gateway (non-standard headers) — those will need explicit routing guidance.

Proposed timeline suggestion (for inclusion in the comm template):
- 2026-12-15: Finalize comms + dependency mapping, publish draft to CSMs.
- 2027-01-15: Start deprecation window (no enforced errors yet, warnings only).
- 2027-04-15: Enforced behavior (errors for unsupported variants) unless exceptions approved.

If a customer files an exception we should have a 14-business-day SLA for triage and a documented escalation path to Product/Infra. Priyom, please confirm intake routing and expected time to decision.

Marissa
Director, Product

I can own the exceptions intake routing and SLA. Operational notes below — copy into the exceptions-intake-form.pdf that Rohan attached: 

- Intake (CSM -> exceptions form) routes to exceptions@redwood.com and auto-creates a ticket in the exceptions board. HubSpot deal ID should be included for business-priority sorting.
- Triage owners: Infra (compatibility), Product (behavioral regression), Legal (contract/terms).
- SLA target: 14 business days for initial decision; if more info needed we'll move to "pending" and request specific artifacts.
- Escalation: Any request flagged as "rollback required" goes to the Escalation Pager and Product leadership for a 72-hour response target.

I've added a lightweight intake field for "technical artifact" links (build logs, example payloads). We'll accept Google Drive links or uploads.

Also — incoming from Acme: forwarding their dependency CSV so we have a sample customer map (attached: acme-dep-list.csv).

Priyom
